name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
alternative_names: Hanging Straight Leg Raise on Captain's Chair
description: The captain's chair straight-leg raise extends the legs fully during the raise, dramatically increasing the lever arm compared to a knee raise and imposing a significantly greater demand on both the rectus abdominis and hip flexors. The long-lever position requires the athlete to control a larger moment of force and recruit more of the lower rectus abdominis to posteriorly tilt the pelvis at the top of the movement. It is a more advanced progression from the knee raise on the same station.

execution.starting_position: Mount the captain's chair with forearms on the pads and back against the pad. Legs hang straight below the body.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure the shoulder pads are positioned to allow the arms to support bodyweight without shrugging the shoulders excessively.
steps: Step 1: Begin with legs hanging straight. Engage the core.
Step 2: Keeping the legs straight (or with a very slight bend at the knees), raise both legs upward until the thighs are at or above horizontal.
Step 3: At the top, curl the pelvis slightly forward (posterior tilt) to maximally engage the lower abs.
Step 4: Lower the legs slowly and with full control back to the hanging position.
Step 5: Avoid swinging — maintain tension throughout the entire set.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as legs rise. Inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs with momentum rather than controlling the full range
Only raising legs to 45° and missing the upper rectus abdominis contribution from posterior pelvic tilt at the top
safety_considerations: Avoid if hip flexor tightness causes anterior pelvic tilt to worsen — use knee raises instead
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Legs from full hang to horizontal or above. Posterior pelvic tilt at the top is essential for full ab engagement.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-1-3-0. Fully controlled. No kipping or swinging.
coaching_cues: Keep legs straight and squeeze the quads
Curl the tailbone up at the top
Resist gravity on the way down
